mainTopic: Converts married to relatives, and widows of mixed-up sons: who does חליצה and who does יבום
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about a man who converts while married to women who would be עריות for a Jew. Following רבי מאיר, relatives connected through the mother must be divorced and relatives through the father may stay. Relatives by marriage, such as a brother's wife, are permitted. The גמרא tries to prove from the ברייתא that a גר may marry a woman his brother married after converting. The proof is pushed off: the brother may have married her as a גוי. The גמרא then explains that the line 'at the outset he should not marry' refers to the wives he was allowed to keep. It ties the two versions about the mother-in-law to רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא. A new משנה follows about five women whose babies got mixed up: each widow gets four חליצות and then one יבום, in a set order and with the brothers taking turns. A ברייתא adds cases with paternal brothers, maternal brothers and כהנים, who may do only חליצה.

steps.title: Father's sister and mother's sister: keep or divorce
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes the case of the father's sister and gives the case of the mother's sister. It then states the general rule of רבי מאיר: a relative through the mother must be divorced, and a relative through the father may stay.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she is his father's sister from the father's side, he may keep her. If she is his mother's sister from the mother's side, he must divorce her. If she is his mother's sister from the father's side, רבי מאיר says he must divorce her, and חכמים say he may keep her. This follows רבי מאיר's rule: any forbidden relative who is connected through the mother must be divorced; if she is connected through the father, he may keep her.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps listing which relatives a convert, who married them before converting, must divorce and which he may keep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר is treated as a newborn, so by Torah law his old family ties are cut. The חכמים still made him divorce some relatives, so people won't say he went from a stricter holiness to a weaker one. Non-Jews already treat relatives through the mother as forbidden, so רבי מאיר says any relative connected through the mother must be divorced, and a relative connected only through the father may stay.

keyTerms.meaning: He may keep her as his wife
He must divorce her (send her out)
A woman forbidden as a close relative

steps.confusionAlert: Under רבי מאיר's rule, a relative counts as 'through the mother' even when she is on the father's side of the family, as long as the link is a mother. For example, the father's sister from the same mother counts this way.

phrases.english: If she is from the father, he may keep her.
phrases.notes: This finishes the case of his father's sister: here she shares only a father with his father.

phrases.english: The mother's sister from the mother: he must divorce her.

phrases.aramaic: מִן הָאָב — רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: יוֹצִיא,
phrases.english: From the father: Rabbi Meir says he must divorce her,
and the Sages say he may keep her.
For Rabbi Meir would say:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עֶרְוָה שֶׁהִיא מִשּׁוּם שְׁאֵר הָאֵם — יוֹצִיא,
phrases.english: Any forbidden relative who is forbidden because of kinship through the mother, he must divorce;
because of the father, he may keep her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relatives connected through the mother must be divorced, and relatives connected through the father may be kept. The חכמים disagree in the case of the mother's sister from the father's side.

steps.title: Brother's wife, uncle's wife and father's wife are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the convert may marry his maternal brother's wife and his father's brother's wife, and all other relatives are permitted too. The גמרא explains that the extra phrase comes to include the father's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is permitted to marry his brother's wife from his mother, and his father's brother's wife. All other forbidden relatives are permitted to him. That last phrase comes to include his father's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists relatives by marriage whom the convert is allowed to marry. The גמרא adds a short note that 'all other relatives' includes the father's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These women are related to him only through marriage, not by blood. So the חכמים saw no reason to forbid them to a גר. The general phrase 'all other relatives' teaches that even the father's wife is included in this permission.

keyTerms.meaning: The wife of his brother who shares only his mother
His father's wife (not his own mother)

steps.whyThisMatters: The line about the brother's wife is the line the גמרא will try to use as a proof in step 4.

phrases.english: And he is permitted to his brother's wife from his mother,
and to his father's brother's wife.
And all the other forbidden relatives are permitted to him.
This comes to include the father's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list, now with relatives by marriage
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר may marry his brother's wife, his uncle's wife and his father's wife.

steps.title: A woman and her daughter
steps.stepSummary: If he was married to both a woman and her daughter, he keeps one and sends away the other. If the daughter died, there are two versions about whether he may keep the mother-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he married a woman and her daughter, he takes back one and divorces the other. From the start he should not marry such a pair. If his wife died, he is permitted to his mother-in-law. Some teach that he is forbidden to his mother-in-law.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא deals with a convert who was married to both a mother and her daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having both together looks too much like a real ערוה, so he may stay with only one. When his wife (the daughter) dies, the first version allows the mother-in-law, and the second version forbids her.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, before the fact
Some teach (another version of the ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא as a whole: blood relatives through the mother are forbidden to a גר. Relatives by marriage, such as a brother's wife, are permitted. A woman and her daughter may not both stay married to him.

phrases.english: If he married a woman and her daughter,
he takes in one and sends away one.
From the start, he should not marry her.
If his wife died, he is permitted to his mother-in-law.
phrases.notes: 'His wife' here is the daughter, so the mother-in-law is the mother who was also married to him.

phrases.english: And some teach: he is forbidden to his mother-in-law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final case of the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He keeps only one of a woman and her daughter. There are two versions about the mother-in-law after his wife dies.

steps.title: Trying to prove a convert may marry his brother's wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא focuses on the line 'permitted to his brother's wife.' It suggests this means even a brother who married her after he converted.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches: he is permitted to his brother's wife. Isn't it talking about a case where his brother married her when the brother was already a גר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the ברייתא as a proof for the question it was discussing before: may a convert marry a woman his brother married after converting?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'his brother's wife' with no limits. So the גמרא suggests it covers even a marriage made after the brother converted. If so, the ברייתא proves such a marriage is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches (focusing on one line)
Isn't it that... (introduces a suggested proof)

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
he is permitted to his brother's wife.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו, דְּנַסְבַהּ אָחִיו כְּשֶׁהוּא גֵּר?
phrases.english: Isn't it that his brother married her when he was a convert?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא just quoted as evidence for the earlier question
steps.raayaObject: That a גר may marry the wife his brother married after converting

steps.title: No, the brother married her as a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the ברייתא may be talking only about a brother who married her before converting.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is a case where he married her when he was a non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by reading the ברייתא as a narrower case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the brother married her while still a גוי, the ברייתא says nothing about a marriage made after conversion. So the question stays open.

phrases.english: No, it is where he married her when he was a non-Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as a marriage made before the brother converted

steps.title: Why would that need to be said?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the brother married her as a non-Jew, it seems obvious that she is permitted, so why teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it coming to tell us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 5, saying it makes the ברייתא state something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A marriage between non-Jews before conversion clearly creates no ערוה. A ברייתא doesn't usually bother to teach obvious things. That weakens the reading of step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the point of saying it? (it's obvious)

phrases.english: What is there to say?
phrases.notes: In other words: that's obvious, so why would the ברייתא need to teach it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the brother married her as a non-Jew
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, the ברייתא would be teaching something obvious

steps.title: No rabbinic decree because of the convert case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: we might have thought the חכמים forbade even the non-Jew case because it looks like the convert case. The ברייתא teaches that they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: let us make a decree forbidding the case where he married her as a non-Jew, because of the case where he married her as a convert. So the ברייתא teaches us there is no such decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point of the ברייתא's line, so the reading of step 5 still works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases look alike, so people might confuse them. Because of that, a גזירה forbidding the non-Jew case was possible. The ברייתא tells us there is no such גזירה. This answer also hints that the case where he married her as a convert is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us make a rabbinic decree

steps.whatToRemember: The proof failed. The ברייתא only permits a brother's wife whom the brother married while still a גוי. Its new point is that there is no גזירה because of the convert case.

phrases.english: You might have said:
Let us decree against when he was a non-Jew
because of when he was a convert;
it teaches us that we don't.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling is not obvious, since a גזירה was possible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים might have forbidden the non-Jew case because it looks like the convert case
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no such גזירה, so a brother's wife married while he was a גוי is permitted

steps.title: Quoting the line about a woman and her daughter again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again: a convert married to a woman and her daughter keeps one and sends away the other, and 'at the outset he should not marry.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: if he was married to a woman and her daughter, he keeps one and sends away the other. At the outset he should not marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again so it can ask about its wording. This step sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already saw this line in step 3. Now the focus is on the last words, 'at the outset he should not marry.' The גמרא wants to know what those words add.

keyTerms.meaning: at the outset, before the fact

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This brings back the ברייתא about converts that the גמרא quoted earlier.

phrases.english: If he married a woman and her daughter
he keeps one and sends away one.
At the outset he should not marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the wording of the ברייתא from step 3, after the discussion about the brother's wife ended in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He keeps one of the two and sends away the other; at the outset he should not marry.

steps.title: Why say 'not at the outset' if he must send her away?
steps.stepSummary: If he has to send her away even after the fact, it is obvious he cannot marry her at the outset, so why say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that he actually has to send her away, do we need to be told that he should not marry her at the outset?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording: the line 'at the outset he should not marry' seems to add nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a marriage that already happened must end, then of course a new one is not allowed. Saying it would be extra. So the גמרא asks what the line really means.

keyTerms.meaning: he actually has to send her away

phrases.english: Now, if he actually has to send her away,
do we need to say he should not marry her at the outset?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the last line quoted in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'לְכַתְּחִלָּה לֹא יִכְנוֹס' in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even after the fact he must divorce, saying he may not marry at the outset is obvious and extra.

steps.title: The line refers back to the case he may keep
steps.stepSummary: The line 'at the outset he should not marry' goes back to the earlier case in the ברייתא, where the convert may stay married.
steps.simpleTranslation: That line refers back to the earlier case, and this is what it means: the one the רבנן said he may keep, he should not marry at the outset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the line is not about the woman and her daughter. It refers back to an earlier case where the convert was allowed to stay married.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that earlier case the רבנן let him keep a wife he already had. Still, he may not marry such a woman for the first time after converting. So the line is not extra; it adds a real limit.

keyTerms.meaning: it stands there, meaning it refers back to an earlier line
and this is what it means
he may keep (stay married to) her

phrases.english: It stands there,
phrases.notes: Meaning the line goes back to an earlier sentence in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: and this is what it is saying:
that one which the Rabbis said he may keep,
he should not marry at the outset.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the line as referring to a different, earlier case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The line seemed to be about the woman and her daughter, which would make it extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The line is about the wife the רבנן allowed him to keep: he may keep her, but may not marry such a woman at the outset.

steps.title: Two versions about the mother-in-law
steps.stepSummary: If his wife died, one version says he may keep his mother-in-law and another says he may not. One version follows רבי ישמעאל and the other follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his wife died, he is permitted to his mother-in-law. Some teach: he is forbidden to his mother-in-law. One follows רבי ישמעאל and one follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes again the two versions about the mother-in-law and says they follow two different תנאים. This step sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions are not a copying mistake; each matches a known view. The next step explains which version follows which תנא and why.

phrases.english: If his wife died,
phrases.notes: His wife here is the daughter, from the woman-and-daughter case.

phrases.english: he is permitted to his mother-in-law.
And some teach:
he is forbidden to his mother-in-law.
One follows Rabbi Yishmael,
and one follows Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, וַחֲדָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the ברייתא, the two versions from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two versions about the mother-in-law follow רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: Why each תנא leads to a different version
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל holds the mother-in-law stays fully forbidden after the wife dies, so the רבנן made a decree for a convert too. רבי עקיבא holds the prohibition gets weaker, so there was no decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who forbids follows רבי ישמעאל, who said the mother-in-law stays forbidden after the wife dies, so the רבנן made a decree for a convert. The one who permits follows רבי עקיבא, who said the prohibition gets weaker after death, so the רבנן did not make a decree for a convert.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how each version matches its תנא. The question is how strong the mother-in-law prohibition is after the wife dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a convert the prohibition comes only from a גזירה of the רבנן. If the prohibition stays strong after death (רבי ישמעאל), the רבנן made the גזירה. If it gets weaker (רבי עקיבא), they did not bother to make one.
steps.whatToRemember: The two versions about the mother-in-law depend on one question: is the prohibition after the wife's death as strong as before (רבי ישמעאל) or weaker (רבי עקיבא)? Only if it stays strong did the רבנן forbid it to a convert.

phrases.english: The one who forbids follows Rabbi Yishmael,
who said: his mother-in-law after death
phrases.notes: 'After death' means after his wife has died.

phrases.english: remains in her prohibition,
and regarding a convert, the Rabbis made a decree about it.
And the one who permits follows Rabbi Akiva,
who said: his mother-in-law after death
her prohibition is weakened,

phrases.aramaic: וְגַבֵּי גֵר לָא גְּזַרוּ בֵּיהּ רַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: and regarding a convert, the Rabbis did not make a decree about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the matching of versions to תנאים stated in step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The version that forbids follows רבי ישמעאל (prohibition stays strong, so a גזירה for converts); the version that permits follows רבי עקיבא (prohibition weakens, so no גזירה).

steps.title: New משנה: five women whose babies got mixed up
steps.stepSummary: Five women's babies got mixed up; they grew up, married, and died. Four brothers do חליצה with one widow, and then one does יבום with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Five women whose babies got mixed up; the mixed-up ones grew up, married women, and died. Four do חליצה for one widow, and one does יבום with her.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It deals with widows when no one knows for sure who their husband's brothers are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we don't know which brother belongs to which dead husband, each widow might be the יבמה of any of them. Four do חליצה to free her from all doubt, and the fifth may then do יבום, since even if she isn't his יבמה she is free to marry him.
steps.confusionAlert: The brothers doing חליצה and יבום are not the mixed-up sons (they died). They are other sons of these mothers whose identity is known.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Five women whose babies got mixed up,
the mixed-up ones grew up and married women,
and died;
four perform halitza for one of the widows,
phrases.notes: The משנה assumes these four are brothers who were not mixed up, each from a different mother.

phrases.english: and one performs levirate marriage with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the convert ended in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the mixed-up sons die, four known brothers do חליצה with each widow, and then one may do יבום with her.

steps.title: The rotation continues until every widow is done
steps.stepSummary: The brother who just did יבום joins three others in doing חליצה for the next widow, and the remaining brother does יבום. In the end, each widow gets four חליצות and one יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then he and three others do חליצה with another widow, and the one left over does יבום with her. In the end, every single widow has had four חליצות and one יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the order of steps from the last line. It moves on to the next widow and then sums up the result for all of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody knows which widow belongs to which brother. So for each widow, four brothers do חליצה and the fifth does יבום. If she is really his sister-in-law, the יבום is fine. If she is not, her real brother-in-law was one of the four, and his חליצה already set her free. Repeating this for every widow covers every possibility.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that releases a widow from the brother-in-law, so she may marry someone else
When the brother of a man who died with no children marries his widow
It turns out; the end result is
For each and every one (of the widows)

steps.whatToRemember: Every widow gets four חליצות and one יבום. That way, whichever brother is really hers, she ends up properly taken care of.

phrases.english: He and three others do חליצה with one (of the other widows),
phrases.notes: 'He' is the brother who just did יבום with the first widow.

phrases.english: and one does יבום with her.
It turns out there are four חליצות and one יבום
for each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא וּשְׁלֹשָׁה חוֹלְצִין לְאַחַת, וְאֶחָד מְיַיבֵּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's procedure that began in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rotate: the previous יבם and three others do חליצה, and a new brother does יבום. In total, each widow receives four חליצות and one יבום.

steps.title: חליצה must come first, then יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from the משנה's order that חליצה must be done before יבום. If יבום came first, a brother might be living with a woman who is still bound to someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The order matters. First they do חליצה, and only then יבום. Doing יבום first is not allowed, because he might be with a יבמה who is still forbidden to outsiders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by pointing out something we learn from the order of the משנה. חליצה has to come first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the brother did יבום before the others did חליצה. If she is not really his sister-in-law, she is still tied to her real brother-in-law. To this brother, she is like any outside woman, and she is forbidden to him. Doing the four חליצות first frees her, so the יבום that follows is permitted whatever the truth is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Specifically; exactly this way and not another
A יבמה who goes with an outsider before she has been released. This is forbidden.

steps.confusionAlert: Even the brother doing יבום counts as an 'outsider' if she turns out not to be his real sister-in-law. That is why the others must do חליצה first.

phrases.english: גמרא:
And specifically, first doing חליצה and then doing יבום,
but doing יבום first, no,
because he would be touching a יבמה who is forbidden to the public.
phrases.notes: Literally 'a יבמה to the market.' It means she is still bound to someone else, so she is off-limits to outsiders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a rule from the order of actions in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חליצה must come before יבום. Doing יבום first risks relations with a יבמה who is still bound to someone else.

steps.title: Why does the brother who did יבום switch to doing חליצה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה rotates the brothers. Why not let one brother do יבום with all the widows?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'he and three others do חליצה with another one'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the משנה's wording. It sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It would seem simpler for the same brother to keep doing יבום while the other four do חליצה each time. So why does the משנה insist that the יבם switch over to doing חליצה?

phrases.english: What is the point of
'he and three others do חליצה with one'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the משנה line covered in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the brothers rotate, instead of one brother doing יבום with every widow.

steps.title: Each brother gets a turn, so he may hit his own sister-in-law
steps.stepSummary: One brother should not do יבום with everyone. Each brother does יבום with one widow, because maybe that one will turn out to be his real sister-in-law.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that you should not think one brother may do יבום with all of them. Instead, each brother does יבום with one widow, because maybe he will happen to get his own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. Rotating gives every brother a chance to do the מצוה of יבום with his true sister-in-law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one brother did all the יבומים, at most one of them could really be his own יבמה. The others would never get a chance at their own. When each brother takes one widow, each has a real chance to do יבום with his actual sister-in-law.

keyTerms.meaning: Happens to come to him; falls to him by chance

phrases.english: So that you should not say one should do יבום with all of them,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא כֹּל חַד וְחַד מְיַיבֵּם חֲדָא,
phrases.english: rather, each one does יבום with one,
maybe his own will happen to come to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The brothers rotate so that each one has a chance to do יבום with his real sister-in-law.

steps.title: A ברייתא: some are brothers and some are not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא adds to the case: if some are brothers and some are not, the brothers do חליצה and the non-brothers do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If some of them are brothers and some are not brothers, the brothers do חליצה and the ones who are not brothers do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that adds a new detail to the משנה's case. Its wording is puzzling, which sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, the ruling sounds backwards. The real brothers only do חליצה, while men who are 'not brothers' do יבום, even though only a brother can do יבום. This strange wording is what the גמרא is about to ask about.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: If some of them are brothers and some of them are not brothers,
the brothers do חליצה,
and those who are not brothers do יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source that adds to the משנה's case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Where some are 'brothers' and some are 'not brothers,' the brothers do חליצה and the non-brothers do יבום.

steps.title: What is the ברייתא saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is puzzled. How can someone who is not a brother do יבום?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא could mean, since its wording seems impossible. This sets up רב ספרא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבום applies only to a brother of the man who died. A ruling that 'non-brothers' do יבום cannot be meant literally, so the words must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying? (asked when wording seems not to make sense)

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the confusing wording of the ברייתא in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What 'brothers' and 'not brothers' mean, since only a brother can do יבום.

steps.title: רב ספרא: maternal brothers do חליצה, paternal brothers do יבום
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא explains that the ברייתא means paternal brothers and maternal brothers. Maternal brothers do חליצה, and paternal brothers do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said, this is what it means: some of them are brothers from the father, and some are brothers from the mother. The brothers from the mother do חליצה, and the brothers from the father do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא answers the question. He explains the ברייתא's 'brothers' and 'not brothers' as brothers through the mother and brothers through the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יבום works only for a brother from the same father. The 'brothers from the mother' here are also related through the father to the mixed-up sons, so any widow might be his real יבמה and he must do חליצה. But she might instead be his sister-in-law only through the mother, who is forbidden to him, so he may not do יבום; the sons who are only paternal brothers do the יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: Brothers with the same father. Only they can do יבום.
Brothers with the same mother. They cannot do יבום.

steps.whatToRemember: יבום only works for brothers from the same father. Here, the brothers who are also maternal brothers of some of the mixed-up sons do only חליצה, because the widow might be their sister-in-law through the mother. The brothers who are only paternal brothers do יבום.
steps.confusionAlert: In everyday speech a maternal brother is a full 'brother.' For יבום, though, only the father's side counts.

phrases.english: רב ספרא said, this is what it means:
Some of them are brothers from the father,
and some of them are brothers from the mother.
The brothers from the mother do חליצה,
and the brothers from the father do יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 19 by explaining the ברייתא's words.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is talking about paternal versus maternal brothers. Maternal brothers do חליצה, and paternal brothers do יבום.

steps.title: Priests do חליצה, non-priests do יבום
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if some of the brothers are כהנים and some are not, the כהנים do חליצה and the non-כהנים do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: If some of them are priests and some are not priests, the priests do חליצה and the ones who are not priests do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the same ברייתא from Step 18. It gives a new case where some of the brothers are כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each widow gets חליצה from several brothers before one brother does יבום. That earlier חליצה might be the real one, and a חלוצה is forbidden to a כהן. So a כהן can only do חליצה, and the יבום has to come from a brother who is not a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: they perform חליצה, the ceremony that frees the widow from יבום
they perform יבום, marrying the brother's widow
a woman who has had חליצה. She is forbidden to a כהן.

steps.confusionAlert: A כהן is allowed to marry a regular widow. The problem here is the חליצה she already had from the other brothers, because a חלוצה is forbidden to a כהן.

phrases.english: Some of them are priests
and some of them are not priests:
the priests perform ḥalitza,
phrases.notes: The widow already had חליצה from other brothers, and a כהן may not marry a woman who had חליצה.

phrases.english: those who are not priests perform levirate marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב ספרא explained the brothers case, the ברייתא moves on to a parallel case with כהנים and non-כהנים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When some of the brothers are כהנים, the כהנים do only חליצה and the non-כהנים do the יבום.

steps.title: Priests and maternal brothers both do only חליצה
steps.stepSummary: If some of the brothers are כהנים and the rest are maternal brothers, no one can do יבום, so they all do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If some of them are priests and some are brothers from the same mother only, both groups do חליצה and none of them do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא combines the two problems we just saw, כהנים and maternal brothers. Since neither group can do יבום, everyone does חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 taught that maternal brothers cannot do יבום, because יבום only applies to paternal brothers. Step 21 taught that כהנים cannot do יבום here, because of the חליצה she already had. In this case no one is left who is allowed to do יבום, so the only option is חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: these and those, meaning both groups

steps.whatToRemember: Only a paternal brother who is not a כהן can do יבום in these mixed-up cases. כהנים and maternal brothers only do חליצה. If nobody fits, everyone does חליצה.

phrases.english: Some of them are priests
and some of them are maternal brothers:
phrases.notes: These are the sons from רב ספרא's explanation in step 20. Any widow might be their sister-in-law only through the mother, so they cannot do יבום.

phrases.english: both these and those perform ḥalitza
and do not perform levirate marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקְצָתָן כֹּהֲנִים וּמִקְצָתָן אַחִין מִן הָאֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the maternal-brother rule from Step 20 with the כהנים rule from Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the brothers are כהנים and maternal brothers, everyone does חליצה and no one does יבום.
